q1_issues.issue: The object-complement small clause "the plan dangerous" is sealed under `Theme` although the instruction set restricts sealing to finite clausal complements, its only non-finite small-clause seal being the impersonal *passive* "is considered / said / thought to be" frame — an active labeling verb with a stated holder is neither.

`Experiencer` for the callers is licensed only on the sealing route ("the holder is `Experiencer` exactly when the complement seals"); on the ordinary tests "call" is an eventive transitive that accepts the progressive, so its subject would be `Agent`.

q2_gaps: Active object-complement small clause with a labeling / speech verb ("call / deem / name X ADJ"): it is not a resultative (the calling does not make the plan dangerous), not a depictive (the state does not merely hold during the calling), and not a finite clausal complement, so the stated qualifier "dangerous" has no licensed carrier.
notes: "The Keepers" is handled exactly per the capitalized-plural-label rule — one Name-only symbol, no GroupOf, no per-member `keeper` typing — and the definite "the plan" correctly projects its typing outside the seal. The sealing choice, though not licensed as written, at least avoids asserting `(Member sk_plan_1 dangerous)` at top level, which is the right non-commitment.
